description: Mirror of window_exhaustion_then_resume.json from the CLIENT's perspective: the client (as DATA sender on a server-opened stream) exhausts the credit the server granted it in welcome.window, MUST NOT send more DATA at window 0, then resumes once a WINDOW update arrives from the server. window is the minimum legal value, 16384, so the numbers stay realistic. send_window mirrors the server twin's assertions (0 at exhaustion, restored to 8192 after WINDOW, back to 0 after the resumed DATA drains it again) so this fixture asserts something real rather than only stream_state. Both send steps require the harness to drive a real app-level Stream.write() (this is not an echo service -- ws-mixer only emits DATA in response to application code writing to a stream), which the Go unit harness (go/wsmixer/sequence_test.go, via Stream.WriteContext) and the conformance runner (conformance/runner/driver, via the adapter's `write` command) both do; only js/test/sequence.test.ts's pure wire-replay loop has no such hook (it only asserts against already-transmitted frames, never calls MixerStream.write()) and skips this one fixture with that reason instead of silently passing it vacuously.
